title: Background alerting silently evaluates New York, not the user's location
description:
CONFIRMED on Evan's Pixel 9, 2026-08-12. Symptom: a Flood Watch issued 08:44 produced no notification; it appeared only as the on-glance banner when he opened the app at 09:50.

Evidence chain:
- alert_settings shows {"safetyNotifications":true} — the user HAS opted in, so the OFF-by-default design is not the cause.
- dumpsys jobscheduler shows the AlertWorker periodic job scheduled and running hourly (last run 4m40s before inspection), so the worker is alive.
- Manifest declares only ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION (granted, foreground-only). ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION is not declared at all, so on Android 10+ LocationManager.getLastKnownLocation returns null (or throws, swallowed by runCatching in LocationProvider) whenever the app is not in the foreground.
- AlertWorker.doWork and AlertWorker.notifySafetyAlerts both resolve location as 'lastKnownLocation() ?: WeatherLocation.DEFAULT', and DEFAULT is New York (40.7128,-74.0060).
- Live NWS at time of diagnosis: Louisville point had Flood Watch severity=Severe (passes SafetyAlerts.filter, which is why the banner showed it) plus a Minor Flood Advisory (correctly filtered). New York point had NO active alerts.
- Stored safety_notified_ids is EMPTY — the worker has never recorded a single qualifying alert, exactly what polling quiet New York produces. Had it polled Louisville it would have recorded the flood watch id and notified.

Scope: this is not only safety alerts. The same fallback feeds the personal-rule evaluation in doWork (snapshot + forecast), so every user-defined rule is being evaluated against New York weather whenever the app is backgrounded. Silent in both cases.

Fix direction: persist the last KNOWN location (written whenever a real fix is obtained in the foreground) and fall back to that before falling back to DEFAULT; DEFAULT should apply only to an install that has never once had a fix. Same root cause as the cold-start cache miss — see the seed's proximity gate. Consider also whether a background-location permission request is warranted, but the persisted-last-location fix works without it.
notes:
FIX COMMITTED 3e087a9: LocationResolver (live fix -> last known -> DEFAULT), wired into HomeViewModel and both AlertWorker sites. 5 unit tests cover the fallback chain. Device-confirmed that last_location_lat/lon/label are now persisted after a foreground open.

STILL UNVERIFIED IN THE FIELD: that a real background poll now uses the remembered location. 'cmd jobscheduler run -f' cannot target WorkManager's namespaced jobs (androidx.work.systemjobscheduler) on Android 17, so a background run cannot be forced on demand. Check after the next natural hourly poll: if safety_notified_ids STILL contains the flood-watch id, the poll saw Louisville (fixed); if it has been wiped to empty, it saw New York. Setting the poll cadence to 15 min in Alerts shortens the wait.
close_reason: VERIFIED IN THE FIELD 2026-08-12. Reproduced the background condition exactly (appops uid COARSE_LOCATION=ignore; rejectTime confirmed the location read was refused during the launch): the app rendered LOUISVILLE, KY with the NWS Louisville Flood Watch, where the pre-fix code would have shown New York. Corroborating: a background AlertWorker run at 14:18 (WorkManager last_enqueue_time; no foreground activity since 11:10) left safety_notified_ids still holding the Louisville flood-watch id — a successful New York poll would have wiped it to empty. appops restored to uid=foreground/package=allow.

title: Maestro cannot reach its on-device gRPC driver — whole suite fails at 0s
description:
Since 2026-08-25, every Maestro flow fails immediately with 'Not able to reach the gRPC server while processing deviceInfo' / 'Command failed (tcp:7001): closed'. All NINE flows fail identically at 0s, including ones untouched for weeks (00-smoke, 02-alerts, 03-gadgetbridge), and the failure happens before any app interaction — so this is the harness, not the app.

The run that died was the first in this session with BOTH the emulator and the developer's Pixel 9 attached over adb.

- Fresh emulator boot (twice), with 2.4GB free beforehand
- adb kill-server / start-server
- adb forward --remove-all
- Extracting maestro-app.apk and maestro-server.apk from ~/.maestro/lib/maestro-client.jar and installing both with 'adb install -r -t' onto the emulator (both reported Success; dev.mobile.maestro and dev.mobile.maestro.test are present) — Maestro still cannot reach the gRPC server, so the instrumentation is not starting or the port forward is not landing

title: Times for a saved place are shown in the DEVICE's timezone, not the place's
description:
Surfaced while verifying the sun module on 2026-08-24. The emulator sits in America/New_York while the location was Mountain View, CA; the glance showed 'Sunrise 9:32 AM / Sunset 10:48 PM'. The instants are CORRECT — 13.2 hours of daylight is right for 37N in late August, and 9:32 EDT is 6:32 PDT — but every time on the screen is formatted with ZoneId.systemDefault(), so a place in another timezone reads three hours off.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: before saved places (just-my-weather-xup) you were nearly always looking at where you physically were, so device zone and place zone agreed and the bug was unreachable. Saving a place in another timezone is now a first-class feature, and checking on somewhere else is arguably the main reason to use it — a parent watching a kid's college town, someone tracking a trip. 'Sunset 10:48 PM' for a place where the sun sets at 7:48 is not a rounding error, it is wrong.

AFFECTED: SunModule (sunrise/sunset via timeFormat), ForecastGrid HourTile (hourFormat), the daily period names come from NWS so they are already place-local, and HomeScreen's 'Observed HH:MM' line.

DESIGN QUESTION worth deciding before coding: show times in the PLACE's zone (what a weather app usually means; needs a zone per saved place — derivable offline from lat/lon only with a timezone-boundary dataset, which is a big asset, OR from the NWS /points response which returns 'timeZone' per grid point and is already fetched and cached), or keep the DEVICE zone and label it. Recommendation: use the NWS-provided timeZone — it is already in a response the app makes, needs no new dependency or asset, and is authoritative for US points.

Acceptance: with a saved place in another timezone, sun times, hourly labels and the observed time all read in that place's local time; the device's own location is unaffected.
close_reason: Fixed: NWS /points timeZone captured through PointsLookup -> point cache -> WeatherSnapshot, and every clock face (sun module, hourly labels, observed line) plus the sun day-rows now read in the place's zone with a safe fallback to the device's. Verified on an Eastern emulator showing Mountain View: 6:32 AM / 7:48 PM, was 9:32 AM / 10:48 PM.

title: Cached-reading freshness cap of 3h is too short for real use — misses the overnight case
description:
CONFIRMED on Evan's Pixel 9, 2026-08-12. He reported still seeing the '…' placeholder on open. The mechanism is NOT broken — verified directly: with the network disabled, a cold start paints the full cached glance from DataStore at +2.56s (LOUISVILLE, KY / 68 / 'Observed 10:35 AM · 26 min ago' / 'Refreshing…'), and the failed fetch correctly keeps the reading with the error line beside Refresh.

The cause is the gate. dumpsys usagestats shows his previous app use ended 2026-08-11 21:49 and the next began 2026-08-12 09:50 — a 12-hour gap. CachedSnapshot.MAX_AGE is 3 hours, so the entry was correctly rejected and he got the placeholder.

The 3h value was chosen (by me, in the original commit) reasoning 'long enough to cover I checked before lunch and again after'. That ignored the dominant real pattern: the first check of the day, after an overnight gap. On this usage the feature can essentially never fire.

The original justification for a tight cap was that the glance showed a bare clock time with no date, so an old reading would read as today's. That justification is now gone: the observation age ships on the same line ('Observed 8:12 PM · 14 hr ago', and '1 day ago' past 24h), so staleness is explicit, and the reading is additionally marked Refreshing… and replaced within about a second.

Fix: raise MAX_AGE so the overnight case works (24h proposed — covers yesterday-morning-to-this-morning while still declining a reading so old it resembles nothing current). Update CachedSnapshotTest boundaries.
close_reason: MAX_AGE raised 3h -> 24h; overnight-gap test added. Mechanism itself verified working on device with network off.

title: Safety alerts: banner on the glance + opt-in notifications

- Minor is mostly marine/nuisance noise: 'Small Craft Advisory' alone was 172 of the 362.

title: Gadgetbridge weather push (Bangle.js 2)
description:

VERIFIED CONTRACT (gadgetbridge.org/internals/development/weather-support, Codeberg wiki, WeatherSpec.java):
- Action: nodomain.freeyourgadget.gadgetbridge.ACTION_GENERIC_WEATHER
- Extra: WeatherJson (String, DEPRECATED but widely supported) or WeatherGz (gzipped UTF-8 JSON, current). Same action string for both.
- UNITS: currentTemp/todayMinTemp/todayMaxTemp in KELVIN; windSpeed in KM/H. currentHumidity percent, windDirection degrees.
- currentConditionCode is an OpenWeatherMap code (803 = broken clouds), NOT an NWS value — needs a mapping layer.
- Android 14+ wants an explicit intent per package. Known targets: nodomain.freeyourgadget.gadgetbridge, .nightly, and com.espruino.gadgetbridge.banglejs (the Bangle.js fork this project will use). targetSdk 35 also needs a <queries> manifest entry or those packages are invisible.

title: ui-flows.sh: ANR check unreachable when the retry fails; no crash detection; brittle temp file
description:

MEDIUM: the ANR check is unreachable on the path where an ANR is most likely. set -e is in force and the retry maestro call is the last command in the then-body, so a failing retry exits the script and the check never runs. Since hide_error_dialogs removes the dialog, an ANR that actually breaks the flows surfaces only as 'assertion timed out' — the diagnostic that exists to explain that shape is skipped exactly then. The check only fired when BOTH passes succeeded, i.e. the narrow 'absorbed by the wait budgets' case. Fix: capture maestro's status, run the diagnostics unconditionally, exit non-zero after.

LOW: hide_error_dialogs suppresses CRASH dialogs too, but only ANR detection was restored. A Java crash after the last assertion of a flow passes green. The crash buffer is already in the dump, unread. Fix: also grep FATAL EXCEPTION scoped to our package.

LOW: the read is fail-closed on adb's exit status, but -b all can exit non-zero after writing everything (one unreadable buffer). Verification covered one image while the script is advertised as locally runnable on arbitrary devices, so a usable dump gets discarded into a red job. That branch also cats the whole file, which with -G 16M can be megabytes into the CI log. Fix: grep a non-empty dump anyway and downgrade to a warning; reserve exit 1 for an empty dump; bound the diagnostic to tail -50.

LOW: predictable temp path opened with > follows a pre-planted symlink on a shared /tmp, and there is no trap, so an interrupted run leaves up to 16 MB behind. Fix: mktemp plus trap EXIT, which also removes the scattered rm -f calls.

title: ui-flows.sh: ANR detector can false-negative; unbounded log window; sticky retry marker
description:
roborev #2956 on d8cb973. Four findings in .github/scripts/ui-flows.sh:

MEDIUM: the post-run ANR check is 'adb logcat | grep -q'. Under set -o pipefail, grep -q exits at the first match, adb dies of SIGPIPE, the pipeline returns non-zero and the if takes the else branch — so an ANR early in the buffer is NOT reported. Position-dependent, inverted exactly on the path the check exists for. Same swallowing hides a broken adb (2>/dev/null).

MEDIUM: -b crash,main are the wrong buffers. ActivityManager emits 'ANR in <pkg>' via Slog (system buffer); the structured am_anr record goes to events. crash carries tombstones, main carries the app's own Log calls. Detector may match nothing on a real ANR.

LOW: the check reads the whole retained log but claims 'during the run' — a locally reused emulator can carry an ANR from an earlier run, and a full suite plus retry can roll the ring buffer past a real one.

LOW: RETRY_MARKER is never cleared at the start, so on a self-hosted runner or local invocation a stale marker makes hashFiles('maestro-retried') != '' true forever, making the artifact upload unconditional again.
close_reason: Closed

title: Hero (observation) and hourly strip (forecast) disagree with no visible provenance
description:
Evan, Louisville, 09:50 local: hero showed 75 deg while the hourly strip showed 9am=71, only reaching 75 at 12pm — reads as the app contradicting itself. VERIFIED NOT AN APP BUG: the two numbers are different NWS products. The hero is a real thermometer reading from the nearest station (KLOU Bowman Field / KSDF); the strip is model output for the 2.5km grid cell. Live check on 2026-08-01 at 10:27 EDT reproduced the same gap from the source: KLOU obs 77.0F (taken 17 min prior), KSDF 78.8F, while the hourly forecast for that same hour said 73F — forecast running ~4 deg cool, generated 14:06Z from a model run updated 10:51Z (hours stale). Textual conditions diverge too (obs 'Mostly Cloudy' vs forecast 'Showers And Thunderstorms Likely').

The real defect is presentation: both numbers are shown with equal authority and no provenance, and the strip's FIRST tile is the current hour, sitting inches from the hero and inviting a direct contradiction. Worse, Evan's density is Spacious, which hides the 'Updated HH:MM' line (Density.showsTimestamp == false for SPACIOUS) — so the one cue that would explain it is suppressed exactly in the calmest view.

Options to weigh: (a) start the hourly strip at the NEXT hour so 'now' is unambiguously the hero's job; (b) always show the observation time regardless of density (or show it whenever the obs/forecast gap exceeds a few degrees); (c) label the two regions (observed vs forecast) once, quietly; (d) some combination. Needs a product call before implementing.
acceptance_criteria: A user cannot read the hero and the first forecast tile as contradicting each other; observation provenance/time is discoverable in every density.

title: Decide place-entry approach for saved locations (lat/lon vs bundled city list vs geocoder)
description:
## Why this needs you (please confirm this is accurate)
`just-my-weather-xup` (Saved/named locations + place picker) is blocked on a product decision only you can make: **how does a user enter a place**, given the app's ethos (no Play Services, no API key, builds from source anywhere)? NWS has no geocoding endpoint, so "type a city name" needs a data source from somewhere. This shapes the dependency footprint and the UX, so I shouldn't pick unilaterally.

## Options
1. **Raw lat/lon entry** — zero dependencies, fully in-ethos, but hostile UX (nobody knows their coordinates).
2. **Bundled US city list** — a small offline dataset (e.g. top ~5k US places from the free GeoNames/Census data, few hundred KB) with a search field. In-ethos (offline, no key), matches NWS's US-only coverage. Adds a data file to maintain. **My recommendation.**
3. **External geocoder API** (Nominatim/OSM or similar) — best UX, but adds a network dependency + usage-policy obligations, and leaks queries off-device. Likely against the ethos.
4. Some combination (e.g. city list with lat/lon as the escape hatch).

## What unblocks me when this returns
A one-line answer ("option 2", or your own variant) and, if a bundled list, any preference on the dataset/size. I'll then implement `just-my-weather-xup`: place entry UI, persistence of saved places, and switching the home view between them.
close_reason: Decided by Evan: option 4 — bundled US Census Gazetteer place list (offline search, public domain) + raw lat/lon entry as escape hatch. No external geocoder.

title: Sun times as a glance module (needs a non-WeatherField module catalog)
description:
The one part of the original fold-in (just-my-weather-8zo) not done when the forecast became the second grid. Sun times is still a two-day table sitting between the two grids rather than a tile the user can place, size and reorder like every other module.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT OUT: the glance grid's config is List<FieldSetting> keyed by the WeatherField enum, and sun times is not a WeatherField — it has no numericValue, is not alertable, and its data comes from SunTimes.daysFrom rather than WeatherSnapshot. Making it one would bend that enum's contract (its doc says 'how to render its value from a WeatherSnapshot') and would put nonsense entries in the alert builder. So this needs a module catalog that admits richer modules alongside value fields, plus a render signature that carries sun data.

DESIGN CARE: do not flatten the two-day table into 'next sunrise / next sunset' to make it fit a value tile. Day rows were chosen deliberately over 'next of each' because between sunrise and sunset those two fall on different dates, and a row carrying its own date says which is which without hanging a 'tomorrow' off a time. A span-adaptive module preserves it: full width draws the table, half/quarter draws a condensed pair.

Acceptance: sun times is a module on the glance grid — placeable, resizable, arrangeable, with the same a11y custom actions as every other tile; the two-day information survives at full width; ViewConfig migration keeps existing showSunTimes users seeing sun times.
close_reason: Shipped in a9afd3c: ModuleKey catalog (Reading/Sun), ModuleContent so a module can carry richer data than a string, span-adaptive sun module preserving the two-day table at full width, showSunTimes migrated into module visibility. 247 unit + 15 instrumented tests and 9/9 Maestro flows pass.

title: Arrange mode: drag directly while wiggling (no second long-press)
description:
Today a reorder always needs hold-then-move, even when the grid is ALREADY in arrange mode. Android's launcher does not: once the icons wiggle, you drag them directly. Adopting that is better UX and it also unlocks automated drag coverage — Maestro 2.5.0 has no hold-then-move gesture (no dragAndDrop; a 2500ms coordinate swipe was probed on-device and never satisfies the long-press), so .maestro/06-arrange.yaml can cover entry, tap-to-cycle, exit and persistence but not the drag itself.

DESIGN CARE REQUIRED — this is why it was not just done: an immediate-drag detector on the grid steals the glance column's vertical scroll while NOT arranging, and keying the detector on `arranging` reintroduces the shipped bug where the pointerInput coroutine is cancelled mid-gesture (the long-press that ENTERS arrange mode flips the key, the drag dies, the tile freezes mid-air). A workable shape: keep detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress on pointerInput(Unit) for the cold-start gesture, add a second detectDragGestures on pointerInput(arranging) so it simply does not exist when not arranging, and guard both against double-handling (bail if a drag is already active) so the two live detectors cannot both accumulate dragPosition.

Acceptance: a plain swipe between two tiles reorders them while arranging; vertical scrolling over the grid is unaffected when not arranging; the cold-start long-press-into-drag still works; 06-arrange.yaml gains a real drag step.

Maestro suite unavailable (just-my-weather-p6t); 06-arrange has the drag step ready.

title: Sun times as day rows, matching the daily forecast
description:
Evan: make sunrise/sunset read like the daily forecast — date directly beside the values, sunrise and sunset in columns, using the same lighter/darker font colours as the daily high/low.

Shape chosen (over 'today only' and 'keep next, date per column'): ONE ROW PER DAY, today and tomorrow. Date tile on the left (weekday over month/day, as the hourly strip's DateTile), then sunrise and sunset columns. Sunrise takes onBackground and sunset onSurfaceVariant, mirroring CombinedDayRow's high/low.

Why this rather than a single row: the NEXT sunrise and the NEXT sunset are on different days for most waking hours — from sunrise until sunset, tonight's sunset is today while the next sunrise is tomorrow — so one date label beside both would be wrong exactly when someone looks. Day rows make each value unambiguous and drop the 'tomorrow' suffix entirely.

Consequences:
- SunTimes gains a per-local-date API (SunDay) and loses SunEvents/next().
- SunLabel and SunLabelTest become dead — the day qualifier they existed for is now the row's date.
- The composable's own ticking clock can go: the ViewModel's minute tick already produces CHANGING state at midnight (the date list shifts), which is what the row tick was compensating for when the events were identical either side of the boundary. That moves the midnight-rollover test from an instrumented test to a JVM one.
- Keep an instrumented test for the em-dash on a missing event (polar night).
close_reason: Shipped in 5eaf60d: SunDay rows with date tile + sunrise/sunset columns, high/low colour pairing; SunTimes gained a per-local-date API; SunLabel removed. Verified on the AVD.

title: Instrumented tests cannot run on Android 17 — Espresso reflects on a removed InputManager method
description:
Running ':app:connectedDebugAndroidTest' against Evan's Pixel 9 (Android 17) fails ALL 9 instrumented tests, including ones untouched by any recent change, with:

  java.lang.NoSuchMethodException: android.hardware.input.InputManager.getInstance []
    at androidx.test.espresso.Espresso.onIdle
    at androidx.compose.ui.test.EspressoLink.runUntilIdle
    at androidx.compose.ui.test.AndroidComposeUiTestEnvironment.runTest

androidx.test.espresso resolves InputManager.getInstance by reflection; that method was removed in Android 17, so every Compose test rule that idles through Espresso dies before the test body runs. This is an environment/dependency incompatibility, not a product defect — the same suite passes on the Pixel_7_API_35 emulator.

Consequence: UI verification must stay on the API 35 AVD for now, and anyone who plugs in a modern device will see a wall of red that looks like a regression. Worth a line in CLAUDE.md's device section once resolved.

Fix direction: bump androidx.test espresso-core / test-runner (currently pulled transitively via the compose BOM 2024.12.01 + androidTestImplementation) to a version that no longer reflects on the removed method, then re-run on both the AVD and a real Android 17 device. Check whether compose-bom needs to move too.
close_reason: espresso-core 3.7.0 + test:runner 1.7.0 + ext:junit 1.3.0 pinned ahead of compose-bom. Verified 11/11 on the Pixel 9 (Android 17), where the suite previously could not start, and 11/11 still on Pixel_7_API_35.

title: Field values read as buttons — pull the value in beside its label
description:
Second report of the same misread: Evan asked what the "Clear button" does and why clicking it did nothing. "Clear" is the Conditions VALUE (NWS textDescription), not a control.

The codebase already carries two mitigations for exactly this, and both were insufficient: DensitySpec.rowMaxWidth is narrowed with the comment 'a lone right-aligned word in a sparse layout reads as a button — Clear (a sky condition) was mistaken for a Clear/reset control', and DateTile avoids the accent colour for 'the same misread that made Clear seem like a control'. Colour already separates them (values are onBackground, controls are accent) and it still was not enough, so the remaining cue is position: FieldRows lays each row out as Row(fillMaxWidth, SpaceBetween) with the value weight(1f) + TextAlign.End, which pins a short value to the far edge of a 240-280dp block, ~150dp from its label. That is the geometry of a settings row with a trailing action.

Fix (chosen by Evan over a tap-to-refresh gesture or pull-to-refresh): pull the value in next to its label so the pair reads as one fact rather than as label + button.

Constraint: FieldRowsTest already pins the width contract this row has regressed against twice — a short label must leave the value most of the row, a runaway custom label must not starve the value, and the cap must follow the real row width. Any change has to keep those green.
close_reason: Value now starts beside its label (FieldRows: spacedBy gap + Start alignment); gap charged to the label budget so FieldRowsTest's value floor still holds. Verified on the AVD.

title: Sunrise/sunset on the glance, as an opt-in element
description:
Show the NEXT sunrise and the NEXT sunset as their own element on the home glance, behind a ViewConfig toggle (off by default, like the other opt-ins).

Data source: computed locally, NOT fetched. NWS does not carry sun times, and adding a second HTTP source for something that is pure astronomy would cost a network dependency, a failure mode, and an offline hole for no accuracy gain. The NOAA solar-position algorithm needs only latitude, longitude and the date, so it is pure, offline, instant, and testable on the JVM — which also means the times still render when the weather fetch fails or the app is showing a remembered reading.

Scope for this first cut (deliberately small):
- Pure SunTimes: next sunrise / next sunset after a given instant, null when the sun does not rise or set within the search window (polar latitudes are a real case, not a hypothetical).
- ViewConfig.showSunTimes flag + codec default false + Customize toggle.
- One dedicated composable on the glance, not a label/value field row — the user asked for its own element, and the WeatherField catalog is the wrong home for it (these are computed, come in a pair, and have no alert-threshold meaning).
- Honest labelling when the next event is not today (e.g. at 11pm the next sunrise is tomorrow's).

Explicitly out of scope for now: day length, golden hour, civil twilight, per-day sun times in the Daily framing, and recomputing while the screen sits open across an event boundary (it recomputes on refresh).
close_reason: Shipped in 559580f: pure SunTimes (USNO-verified), ViewConfig.showSunTimes opt-in, dedicated glance element, SunLabel day qualifier. Verified on the API 35 AVD.

title: Point cache is keyed on raw jittering coordinates — 17 entries for one location, grows forever
description:
Observed in the field on Evan's Pixel 9, 2026-08-12. The persisted point_cache held 18 entries, 17 of them the SAME place:

  40.7128,-74.006                      -> OKX/KNYC   (New York, from the background-location bug, see just-my-weather-jsu)
  38.252252252252255,-85.6806540212635 -> LMK/KLOU
  38.252252252252255,-85.68068173281894 -> LMK/KLOU
  38.252252252252255,-85.6804653663773 -> LMK/KLOU
  ... 14 more, all LMK/KLOU

WeatherRepository.resolvePoint keys on "${lat},${lon}" at full double precision. ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION quantises latitude (hence the constant 38.252252252252255) but the longitude carries a randomised offset that Android regenerates roughly hourly, so nearly every launch produces a brand-new key.

Two consequences:
1. The cache mostly misses. Each new key costs a fresh /points AND /stations round trip on launch — exactly the two calls the cache exists to avoid. All 17 keys resolve to the same grid (LMK 2.5km cell) and the same station (KLOU).
2. It grows without bound. Nothing evicts, and the whole map is re-encoded to JSON and rewritten to DataStore on every put, so the write cost climbs with use.

Fix: round the key to the resolution that actually matters. An NWS grid cell is ~2.5 km, so 2 decimal places (~1.1 km) is already finer than the data; 3 dp is conservative. Rounding to 2 dp would have collapsed all 17 entries into one. Consider also a modest cap/eviction so a genuinely mobile user does not accumulate entries forever.

Note the fix interacts with just-my-weather-jsu: with a persisted last-known location the resolver returns a stable coordinate more often, which reduces but does not remove the churn — a live fix still jitters.
close_reason: Key rounded to 2dp (17 observed keys collapse to 1), legacy keys dropped on load, cache bounded at 32 oldest-first; Locale.ROOT and negative-zero handled. All four behaviours verified to fail against reintroduced defects.

title: Flaky instrumented test: FieldRowsTest 'No compose hierarchies found' on a cold run
description: Seen once on 2026-08-07 during the ObservedLine work: FieldRowsTest.aShortPairIsNotStretchedApart failed with IllegalStateException 'No compose hierarchies found in the app... the Activity that calls setContent did not launch'. It was the first connectedDebugAndroidTest run after a fresh emulator boot + test APK install. NOT reproduced in 4 subsequent runs (once before and three times after adding an @After autoAdvance restore to ObservedLineTest), and FieldRowsTest passes in isolation. So the trigger is unconfirmed: candidates are (a) an activity-launch race on the first cold run of the test process, or (b) ObservedLineTest leaking a paused Compose test clock into a following test — it pauses mainClock and leaves an endless ticker parked on a delay. The @After restore was added as insurance, but it is NOT established as the fix since the failure was already non-reproducing. If this recurs in CI, capture whether ObservedLineTest ran before FieldRowsTest in that run — that distinguishes (a) from (b).
notes:
NEW EVIDENCE 2026-08-15, and a likely cause for the physical-device case. Running :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest on the Pixel 9 (now possible, see just-my-weather-1te) failed 2 of 11 with the same 'No compose hierarchies found in the app ... the Activity that calls setContent did not launch'. Immediately afterwards the device reported mWakefulness=Dozing and isKeyguardShowing=true: the screen slept and re-locked mid-run (screen_off_timeout was 60s; the build+install+run exceeds that idle window). A locked, dozing device cannot launch the test activity, which is exactly what the message says.

So on a real device the fix is procedural, not code: keep it awake for the duration — 'adb shell svc power stayon usb' before the run and 'svc power stayon false' after — and make sure it is unlocked when the run starts.

This does NOT explain the original emulator sighting (2026-08-07, FieldRowsTest), where nothing was sleeping; that one remains unreproduced after many runs. Same symptom, possibly two different causes — an activity that fails to launch for any reason produces this message. Worth adding the stayon step to the device workflow in CLAUDE.md if instrumented runs on hardware become routine.
close_reason: Obsolete: FieldRowsTest was deleted in 39aad42 with the row layout it asserted; the module grid's instrumented coverage is tracked in just-my-weather-duo

title: Show observation age on the glance ("Observed 12:40 PM · 12 min ago")
description:
Evan asked why the Observed time doesn't change when hitting Refresh. It is expected — that line is the STATION's observation time, not the fetch time, and refresh genuinely re-fetches (only the grid/station lookup is cached; OkHttp has no HTTP cache). Verified live 2026-08-03: KLOU/KSDF publish every 5 min, NWS serves /observations/latest with cache-control max-age=183, s-maxage=300, and at 12:52 PM the newest record was 12:40 PM with temperature flat across the previous six observations.

Now documented in three places (HomeScreen.observedLabel, README 'Data & privacy', docs/architecture.md 'Freshness'), so this is NOT about explaining it again.

The real gap is feedback: pressing Refresh and seeing nothing move gives no confirmation the fetch happened, and a genuinely stale station is indistinguishable from a working one. Proposed: render the AGE alongside the timestamp rather than replacing it — 'Observed 12:40 PM · 12 min ago'. That answers 'is this current?' without adding a second timestamp (a separate checked-at line would re-add the chrome consolidated in f6524c9 and risks reading as two contradictory times).

Design notes: the age has to recompute over time or it goes stale itself while the screen is open, so it needs a ticking source rather than a value computed once at render. Keep it out of the Gadgetbridge payload — that carries the raw epoch and the watch does its own formatting.
close_reason: Age renders beside the timestamp ('Observed 1:51 PM · 36 min ago'), ticks every 30s; pure ObservationAge tested on JVM, verified on the API 35 AVD

title: Alerting: per-rule tone/vibration + snooze
description:
## Why this needs you

Three product calls, and one of them is effectively irreversible. On Android 8+
sound and vibration are properties of the **notification channel**, not the
notification, and a channel's settings cannot be changed after it is created.
So "per-rule tone" means shipping one channel per tone (doubled, because there
is already a quiet variant), created up front and named so they read sensibly
in the system settings list. Once users have tuned those channels they cannot
be renamed or repurposed — a wrong guess here is a permanent wart in everyone's
notification settings.

## Decide

1. **How many tones?** Each option is a permanent channel pair. My
   recommendation: three — *Default*, *Silent*, and one *Alternative* — giving
   channels: Alerts / Alerts (silent) / Alerts (alternative), each with a quiet
   -hours twin. Fewer is safer than more; adding a tone later is easy, removing
   one is not.
2. **What does Snooze mean?** Rules re-evaluate on every poll, so without
   persisted state a snoozed alert simply returns on the next check.
   - (a) **Per-rule, persisted** — "stop telling me about the overnight low
     until 6am". Survives the poll, survives a reboot. More code (state +
     expiry), and the honest reading of "snooze".
   - (b) **Per-notification only** — dismisses this post; the next poll may
     re-post it. Cheap, and arguably a lie.
   My recommendation: (a).
3. **Snooze durations** — which options appear on the notification action?
   Suggest 1h / until tomorrow morning; more than two actions crowds the
   notification.

## What unblocks me

Answer 1–3 in a comment here (or just "go with your recommendations") and
remove the `human` label. I will then implement: `AlertRule` gains a tone
field, `AlertNotifier` creates the channel matrix up front and routes by tone,
snooze state persists alongside the rules, and a `BroadcastReceiver` handles
the notification action.

## Files involved

- `app/src/main/java/io/raylytics/justmyweather/alerts/AlertRule.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/io/raylytics/justmyweather/alerts/AlertNotifier.kt`
  (creates `CHANNEL_ID` and `QUIET_CHANNEL_ID` today)
- `app/src/main/java/io/raylytics/justmyweather/alerts/AlertRulesCodec.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/io/raylytics/justmyweather/ui/alerts/AlertsScreen.kt`

## Prior description (preserved on handoff)

Second half of just-my-weather-pcj, split out once the quiet-window picker landed (a7d5f96 era). The window half is done; this is the part with real design work.

WHY IT IS BIGGER THAN IT LOOKS:
- AlertRule has no tone field today (id, subject, comparison, threshold, enabled, window).
- AlertNotifier creates exactly two channels at startup: CHANNEL_ID (IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT) and QUIET_CHANNEL_ID (IMPORTANCE_LOW, setSound(null,null)). On Android 8+, sound and vibration are properties of the CHANNEL, not the notification, and channel settings are immutable after creation — so per-rule tone means one channel per tone (x2 for the quiet variant), created up front and named so they read sensibly in system settings. Changing a tone later cannot mutate a channel; it has to move the rule to a different one.
- Snooze needs a notification action + PendingIntent + a BroadcastReceiver, and a decision about what snooze MEANS here: suppress this rule's re-notification until a time, or suppress the notification only? Rules re-evaluate on a poll, so without state a snoozed alert simply returns on the next check.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR A PRODUCT CALL: how many tone options (system default / silent / one alternative?), snooze durations, and whether snooze is per-rule state (persisted) or per-notification.

Suggest scoping this properly before implementing — the channel-per-tone consequence is the kind of thing that is annoying to undo once it ships, because channels users have already tuned cannot be renamed or re-purposed.

title: ui-flows.sh: trap armed after both mktemps; watchdog discards adb stderr
description:
roborev #2984 on 63e0917 — both regressions introduced by the stderr-split fix.

LOW: the trap was installed after BOTH mktemp calls, so a failing second mktemp (full or unwritable TMPDIR) exits under set -e with the first file created and no trap to remove it. Reproduced with a stub mktemp failing on call 2: committed version leaves 1 orphan, fixed version 0. Trap is now armed between the two mktemps; its body reads ANR_ERR via ${ANR_ERR:-} so firing early is harmless.

LOW: the 60s watchdog branch was the only failure path not surfacing ANR_ERR. Before the stream split adb's stderr at least reached the dump; after it the clue was discarded exactly where a human most needs the cause. Reproduced with a stub writing 'error: device offline' then wedging. Added the same guarded echo the other failure paths use.
close_reason: Closed

title: ui-flows.sh: adb stderr folded into the logcat dump counted as evidence
description: roborev #2978 on 6471d6c. LOW: the read was >"$ANR_DUMP" 2>&1, so adb's own failure text landed in the dump. 'error: device offline' is ~24 bytes, so the dump was non-empty, passed the emptiness gate, and both greps found no ANR in what was never a log buffer — green on a check that never read one. Fixed at the source by sending stderr to its own mktemp'd file rather than adding a downstream log-shape regex, which could false-negative on a device formatting timestamps differently and turn a usable partial dump into a hard failure.
close_reason: Closed

title: ui-flows.sh: empty logcat dump with rc=0 fails open; split idioms; MAESTRO_RC dropped on early exits
description:
roborev #2973 on ffbce0c. Three Lows:

LOW: the 'judge on the dump, not the status' rule was only enforced on the READ_RC != 0 branch. A logcat that exits 0 having written nothing makes both greps report no match, and the run is declared clean on no evidence — the exact fail-open the comment claimed to close. Test emptiness first, independent of status.

LOW: the two halves of the same check used different idioms side by side. The crash half captures into a variable and matches with case (and the file's own comment argues that is correct because grep|grep is the pipefail race); the ANR half still grepped the file twice and piped into head -5, needing a || true escape hatch and a three-line comment. Legibility is the spec here, so make both one shape.

LOW: the 'device is gone' and 60s-watchdog exits report only that the check did not run, silently discarding MAESTRO_RC. The premise of the previous commit is that the flow result and the diagnostics are separate facts; dropping one on the path where the device vanished mid-run loses the more actionable half.
close_reason: Closed

title: Conditions value ('Clear') reads as a tappable button
description:
Evan asked 'what should hitting Clear do? It doesn't do anything.' Correct — 'Clear' is not a control, it is the VALUE of the Conditions field (sky condition from the station's textDescription), rendered as the right-hand side of a label-value row in HomeScreen's NowContent. It does nothing because it is static text.

The affordance is genuinely misleading though: a lone right-aligned word in a sparse layout reads as a button, and the word 'Clear' is itself a common action verb (clear/reset), which makes it the worst possible case. Colour already differentiates (values use onBackground, actions use the accent), but that was not enough to prevent the misread — and it will be weaker for users on accent colours with lower contrast, or for anyone scanning quickly.

Options: (a) leave it (values are already colour-differentiated); (b) tighten the value's typography/alignment so label-value rows read as a unit rather than as label+control; (c) reserve the accent colour exclusively for interactive elements and ensure no value ever borrows it; (d) revisit the row layout (e.g. value directly under label, or a middle dot separator) so nothing sits alone at the right edge. Small, but it is a first-impressions bug in the app's single most-looked-at screen.
acceptance_criteria: A first-time user does not attempt to tap a field value on the home glance.
close_reason: Closed

Add a CI job using reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner to boot an emulator, install the debug APK, and run the Maestro flows. Keep it a separate job from the fast gate so unit-test feedback stays quick; consider running it on main pushes only if PR wall-clock cost is too high.

Added .maestro/02-alerts.yaml covering the highest-state screen (build rule, toggle, quiet hours, remove, return), which required the testTags noted in this issue — quietHours/toggleRule/removeRule/thresholdValue/addRule on AlertsScreen. 3/3 flows pass locally in 43s and BOTH CI jobs passed on the first run (run 30720221115). title: Saved/named locations + place picker
description: The app currently shows the device's coarse location or falls back to WeatherLocation.DEFAULT (New York); there's no way to pick or save a named place, and the README overstated this ('set a place by hand'). Add the ability to choose/save one or more places. OPEN DESIGN QUESTION for a human: how to enter a place given the app's ethos (no Play Services, no API key, builds from source)? Options: (a) raw lat/lon entry, (b) a bundled US city list, (c) an external geocoder (adds a key/dependency — likely against the ethos). NWS has no geocoding. Was the remaining scope of the closed iy0 persistence epic.
design: Place entry (decided in just-my-weather-dww): bundled offline gazetteer + lat/lon escape hatch. (1) Data: US Census Gazetteer 'Places' file (~32k incorporated places + CDPs, includes PR/VI/GU/AS/MP, public domain). Prep script in scripts/ (regeneratable by contributors) trims to name,state,lat,lon at 2-decimal precision (~1.1km, inside NWS 2.5km grid) → asset ~1MB raw / ~400KB compressed. (2) UI: search-as-you-type over the in-memory list; 'enter coordinates' row at the bottom as the escape hatch for unlisted spots. (3) Persist saved places via DataStore (existing codec pattern), each a WeatherLocation(lat,lon,label); home view switches between saved places and the coarse-location fix. No network calls, no attribution requirements.
close_reason: Shipped in 6de036f (committed, push blocked on SSH key — see handoff): bundled US Census gazetteer (32,104 places, 840KB asset + scripts/build-gazetteer.sh), pure ranked search, saved places with DataStore persistence, coordinate escape hatch, and LocationResolver preferring a chosen place over the device fix so background alerts follow it too.
